summary.oneLiner: Sambhv Steel delivered a landmark Q4FY26 with PAT doubling to INR 56 Cr and EBITDA/ton peaking at INR 9,500 driven by low-cost raw material inventory and strong realizations. The company is aggressively expanding capacity toward a 2 Mn ton target by 2030, leveraging PLI incentives and captive power to sustain margins despite rising input costs.

one-line thesis: Sambhv Steel delivered a landmark Q4FY26 with PAT doubling to INR 56 Cr and EBITDA/ton peaking at INR 9,500 driven by low-cost raw material inventory and strong realizations. The company is aggressively expanding capacity toward a 2 Mn ton target by 2030, leveraging PLI incentives and captive power to sustain margins despite rising input costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 685 Cr (+38% YoY); EBITDA: INR 92 Cr (+91% YoY), Margin 13% (vs ~11% FY26 avg); PAT: INR 56 Cr (>100% YoY), Normalized for one-off inventory gains from low-cost Q3 procurement; Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but demand cited as robust across infrastructure; Net Debt: Peak long-term debt guided at INR 800 Cr + INR 200-300 Cr WC post-capex.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Volume growth 10-15% in FY27; Margin: EBITDA/ton INR 7,500-8,000 sustainable in FY27 (Q4 peak of 9,500 due to inventory lag); Order Inflow: Strong demand from solar, warehousing, railways; Capex/Commissioning: Kesda Phase 1 (3.6 L ton SS) by Q4FY27; Brownfield SS debottlenecking (1.16 L ton) immediate.
order book & pipeline: Management cites strong demand visibility from government capex (railways, metros, airports, solar 500GW target) but does not disclose a specific numeric order book value; utilization targets imply healthy fill-rates (SS 60-65%, MS 65-70%, GP 80-90%).
segment / subsidiary detail: Carbon Steel: ERW pipes/tubes, GP pipes/coils; Stainless Steel: CR coils (200/300 series), expanding to 400 series; Value-add: Co-branding MOUs (10 live) for pipe manufacturing.
growth verticals / optionality: 2 Mn ton finished steel capacity by 2030 (10 L ton MS pipes, 3 L ton coated, 7 L ton SS); Greenfield Kesda project (Phase 1: 3.6 L ton SS); Potential seamless pipe entry under PLI 1.2 pending approvals.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA/ton INR 9,500 inflated by Q3 low-cost raw material (iron ore/coal) usage; FY27 guidance INR 7,500-8,000/ton; Power cost savings of INR 60-70 Cr expected from new captive plants; Raw material pass-through estimated at 50-60% of realization hikes.
capex / expansion: Total identified capex INR 1.13k Cr (INR 930 Cr Kesda Phase 1 + INR 200 Cr operational efficiency/power/DFT); Funding: INR 675 Cr term loan for Kesda, balance internal accruals/debt; Additional INR 300-400 Cr potential capex by FY28 for undefined Phase 2/3.
capital allocation: Debt prudence policy: Long-term debt <1.5x Net Worth and <1.5x Forward EBITDA; INR 100 Cr parked in liquid mutual funds (current investments); Focus on internal accruals for incremental efficiency capex.
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (iron ore/coal); Execution risk on 2 Mn ton expansion; Working capital cycle elongation (guided to 25-30 days) as SS mix increases; Geopolitical impacts on energy/logistics (mitigated by captive power/LNG).
management quality / tone: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'Sambhv hai, toh sab sambhv hai' (If Sambhv exists, everything is possible); Prudent on debt but aggressive on volume/market share targets (10-12% share in MS/SS by 2030).
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory accounting method (WIP valued at cost) neutralizes stock profit/loss volatility; DFT technology reduces size-changeover time from 3-4 hours to near-instant, boosting effective capacity by 10-12k ton/month per machine; PLI incentive capped at ~INR 200 Cr or tonnage, providing a 13-15% revenue boost on eligible thin-gauge production.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising raw material costs and energy prices squeezing non-integrated peers | Sambhv Steel Tubes Ltd | beneficiary | High | Captive power (100% self-sufficiency at Sarora, partial at Kesda) and in-house iron ore/coal sourcing insulate margins; PLI scheme adds 13-15% incentive on high-value SS production. |

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.
themes.driver: Capex commissioning converting to volume; solar-structure & infra demand; commodity pass-through.
